items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: I learned a lot of things from Louis actually because I would watch him, you know, and I learned an awful lot watching Louis and listening to him

ctx.x: Yesterday we were talking about Earl Hines and some of the members of the band (inaudible). I think we started to talk about Walter Fuller.

Yes, we did. And Walter was a very fine trumpet player with Earl and he was a good singer. He sang, you know, he had a jazz style of singing. And he tried to pattern somewhat after Louis, Louis Armstrong. But he had a high voice, a much higher voice than Lou. And he sang things with Earl, some of his popular things. "Rosetta" was one thing I remember in particular. It was a very popular record that Earl had out. And Walter Fuller sang the chorus on this. And it was a wonderful chorus that he did. In fact, they…
and he was doing quite a bit of playing with different groups over in Europe. And whenever an artist came to Europe and he didn't bring his own band, well, he would back him over in Europe.
